questions.question: Which of the following articles deal with Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 36-51**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 36-51** deal with the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Directive Principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, aiming to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down therein are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Directive Principles emphasize that the state should strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all the institutions of national life.
 
• They cover a wide range of social and economic rights, including the right to work, to education, to public assistance in certain cases, and to just and humane conditions of work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: The All-India Muslim League, popularly known as the Muslim League, was founded in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1906**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The All-India Muslim League**, popularly known as the Muslim League, was founded in **1906**.
 
• The Muslim League played a crucial role in Indian politics during the British Raj and was instrumental in the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
 
• The founding of the Muslim League marked the beginning of a significant movement for the political rights of Muslims in India.
 
• The party was established to address the concerns of the Muslim community and to promote their political interests.
 
• It served as a platform for articulating the demands and aspirations of Muslims, particularly in the context of the broader Indian nationalist movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Muslim League** was founded in Dhaka, which was then part of British India and is now the capital of Bangladesh.
 
• Its formation was influenced by a sense of insecurity among Muslims regarding their position in Indian society, especially in the face of the rising Indian National Congress.
 
• Key figures in the establishment of the Muslim League included Nawab Khwaja Salimullah, Aga Khan III, and other prominent Muslim leaders.
 
• Over time, the League's demand evolved from seeking separate electorates for Muslims to advocating for a separate nation, leading to the creation of Pakistan.
 
• The party's resolution for the creation of Pakistan was formalized in the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

questions.question: In which year was the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council abolished?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2019**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished in **2019**.
 
• This move was part of the reorganization of the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The reorganization involved the bifurcation of the state into two Union Territories: **Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh**.
 
• The legislative changes aimed to bring uniformity in governance and improve administrative efficiency in the region.
 
• The abolition of the Council was intended to streamline the legislative process within the newly formed Union Territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The reorganization of Jammu and Kashmir was effected through the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.
 
• Prior to its abolition, the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was the upper house of the bicameral legislature in the state.
 
• The decision to abolish the Council was taken to reduce redundancy and enhance legislative efficiency.
 
• The **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 **was passed by the Parliament of India and received the President's assent on August 9, 2019.

questions.question: Which vitamin prevents the neural tube defect in new-born babies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Folic acid**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Folic acid** is a type of B vitamin that is crucial for preventing neural tube defects in new-born babies.
 
• Neural tube defects are serious birth defects of the brain and spine, such as spina bifida and anencephaly.
 
• Folic acid helps in the formation of the neural tube during the early stages of pregnancy.
 
• It is recommended that women take folic acid supplements before conception and during early pregnancy to ensure proper neural tube development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ascorbic acid**, commonly known as Vitamin C, is essential for collagen synthesis and immune function.
 
• **Riboflavin**, or Vitamin B2, is crucial for energy production and cellular function.
 
• **Niacin**, or Vitamin B3, supports metabolism, DNA repair, and skin health.

questions.question: Who requested the Syrian king to send a Greek philosopher?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindusara** was the second Mauryan emperor of India.
 
• Bindusara ruled from approximately **297 BCE to 273 BCE**.
 
• He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the father of Ashoka.
 
• Bindusara requested the Syrian king Antiochus I to send a Greek philosopher to his court.
 
• This request indicates the cultural and intellectual exchanges between the Mauryan Empire and the Hellenistic world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• He founded the Maurya Empire in ancient India, he established a centralized state and united most of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He ruled from **321 to 297 BCE **and was advised by the strategist **Kautilya**, also known as **Chanakya**.
 
• His reign marked the beginning of one of India’s largest empires.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka:**
 
 
• Grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, he ruled the Maurya Empire from **268 to 232 BCE **and is renowned for his promotion of **Buddhism and non-violence**.
 
• After witnessing the devastation of the **Kalinga War**, he embraced and propagated moral and ethical governance.
 
• His edicts, inscribed on pillars and rocks, reflect his commitment to justice and welfare.

questions.question: In which of the following years, was the Self-Respect movement started in Tamil Nadu region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1925**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Self-Respect Movement was started in the year **1925**.
 
• It was founded by **E.V. Ramasamy, popularly known as Periyar**.
 
• The movement aimed at achieving a society where backward castes have equal human rights, and encouraging backward castes to have self-respect in the context of a caste-based society that considered them to be at the lower end of the hierarchy.
 
• It also sought to eliminate the influence of Brahminism and the caste system in Tamil society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Self-Respect Movement was pivotal in shaping the socio-political landscape of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It advocated for women's rights, including the right to education and the right to choose their partners.
 
• Periyar's efforts laid the foundation for the Dravidian movement, which has had a lasting impact on Tamil Nadu's politics.
 
• The movement also promoted the use of Tamil language and culture over the imposition of Sanskrit and Hindi.
 
• Periyar's work continues to be celebrated and remembered in Tamil Nadu and beyond.

questions.question: Who among the following was the guru of Tansen?

• **Swami Haridasa** was the guru of Tansen, one of the greatest musicians in Indian history.
 
• Tansen was a prominent figure in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar and is often credited with creating the classical music genre known as the Hindustani classical music.
 
• Swami Haridasa was a renowned saint and musician who greatly influenced Tansen's musical style and technique.
 
• Swami Haridasa is also known for his devotion to Lord Krishna and his compositions in praise of the deity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tansen's real name** was Ramtanu Pandey, and he was born in a Hindu family in Gwalior.
 
• He initially served in the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa, where his talent was recognized and later led to his invitation to Akbar's court.
 
• Swami Haridasa's teachings were instrumental in Tansen's development as a musician, which eventually led him to become one of the "Navaratnas" (Nine Gems) in Akbar's court.
 
• Swami Haridasa's legacy continues to influence Indian classical music, and he is revered as a significant figure in the Bhakti movement.

questions.question: According to Hindu calendar, on which day does Holika Dahan take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phalgun Poornima**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Holika Dahan** takes place on **Phalgun Poornima**, which is the full moon day in the month of Phalgun according to the Hindu calendar.
 
• This festival marks the victory of good over evil and is celebrated by lighting bonfires.
 
• The bonfire signifies the burning of the demoness Holika, who was defeated by the devotee Prahlad with the help of Lord Vishnu.
 
• Holika Dahan is an important ritual preceding the festival of Holi, the festival of colors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Holi** is celebrated on the day following Holika Dahan and is one of the most vibrant festivals in India.
 
• The festival signifies the arrival of spring and the end of winter, and for many, it is a festive day to meet others, play and laugh, forget and forgive, and repair broken relationships.
 
• Holi celebrations start on the night before Holi with Holika Dahan where people gather, perform religious rituals in front of the bonfire, and pray that their internal evil be destroyed the way Holika was killed in the fire.
 
• The next morning is celebrated as Rangwali Holi – a free-for-all festival of colors, where people smear each other with colors and drench each other.
 
• Water guns and water-filled balloons are also used to play and color each other.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms of India is a blend of dance, music and acting and dramatises stories, which are mostly adapted from the Indian epics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance form of India that is a blend of dance, music, and acting.
 
• This dance form is known for its elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and detailed gestures.
 
• Kathakali primarily dramatizes stories from Indian epics such as the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.
 
• It originated in the southwestern state of Kerala and has a rich tradition and cultural significance.
 
• The performances are usually conducted in the evenings and can last for several hours, often all night.
 
• Kathakali combines elements of literature, music, painting, and acting, making it a comprehensive art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri** is another classical dance form from the northeastern state of Manipur, known for its graceful movements and themes based on the love story of Radha and Krishna.
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form from the eastern state of Odisha, characterized by its fluid movements and sculpturesque poses.
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form from northern India, known for its intricate footwork and spins, often narrating stories through expressive gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Each of these dance forms has its unique style, history, and cultural significance, contributing to the rich tapestry of Indian classical dance.

questions.question: Who has the power to prorogue the House or either House of State Legislature from time to time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power to prorogue the House or either House of the State Legislature from time to time is vested in the **Governor**.
 
• This power is part of the Governor's broader role in the legislative process, which includes summoning and dissolving the state legislative assembly.
 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the state's Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers but retains certain discretionary powers.
 
• The ability to prorogue the legislature helps in managing the legislative calendar and addressing situations where the House may need to be temporarily suspended.
 
• Proroguing the House effectively ends a session but does not dissolve the legislative assembly, allowing for the continuation of the legislative process in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Governor** is appointed by the President of India and acts as the central government's representative in the state.
 
• The Governor's role is outlined in the **Constitution of India**, particularly in Articles 153 to 167.
 
• The Governor has both executive and legislative powers, including giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature, issuing ordinances, and making recommendations for President's Rule in the state.
 
• In addition to proroguing the House, the Governor can also dissolve the legislative assembly, usually upon the advice of the Chief Minister.
 
• The **Governor** plays a crucial role in maintaining the constitutional framework and ensuring the smooth functioning of the state government.
